title: AgentTrek: Agent Trajectory Synthesis via Guiding Replay with Web Tutorials
data_curation: This is the paper's central contribution. The pipeline mines tutorials from the RedPajama corpus (20.8B entries) in four steps: (1) a rule-based pre-filter (keyword/length/URL heuristics, 200-5000 words) cuts it to 68.8M entries at 92.69% recall; (2) GPT-4o-mini labels 90K samples as tutorial/non-tutorial (F1 88.5%); (3) a FastText classifier trained on those labels (F1 89.5%) filters to ~18.8M deduplicated entries; (4) GPT-4o-mini standardizes each into a template (Platform, Task Description, Prerequisites, Step-by-Step Instructions, Expected Outcome) at $0.89/1K. A VLM agent (GPT-4o-08-06) then replays tutorials in real browsers via BrowserGym (~8,027 tokens/step, 86,114/task, $215/1K tasks), recording screenshots, AXTree, DOM, reasoning, and Playwright actions. A GPT-4o VLM evaluator (84% accuracy vs a 1,081-trajectory human gold set) filters trajectories. Output: 23,430 filtered tutorials yielding 10,398 verified trajectories across 127 websites and 11 categories, averaging 12.1 steps, at $0.551 per trajectory.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is single-stage supervised fine-tuning with no pretrain->SFT->preference/RL ordering: Qwen2-VL is fine-tuned on 10,000 visual trajectories, and Qwen2.5-7B/32B LLMs are fine-tuned on 6,000 textual (AXTree + Playwright action) trajectories. The only cross-stage mixing note is that combining AgentTrek trajectories with Mind2Web human-annotated data yields the strongest Multimodal-Mind2Web results, suggesting the two sources are complementary (AgentTrek supplies grounded interaction, Mind2Web adds specialized complex-task data).
method: The core method is 'guided replay with web tutorials' for synthesizing GUI-agent trajectories. Instead of giving a VLM agent only a high-level goal, the agent is handed a standardized tutorial (target URL plus step-by-step instructions) and executes it in live web environments via BrowserGym, with the agent emitting an inner-thought reasoning chain before each Playwright action. The key empirical trick: in a 400-task controlled experiment, tutorial-guided replay achieves 52% success (208 effective trajectories) versus 15.78% (63) for goal-only guidance, a 23-point gain attributed to direct target URLs, human-style planning, and menu navigation help. Quality control uses a GPT-4o VLM evaluator scoring task adherence and component completion at trajectory, step, and earliest-failure levels. For vision agents the pipeline maps Playwright actions to pyautogui pixel commands; for text agents it uses AXTree observations with bid element IDs. Qwen2-VL uses a NaViT image encoder for dynamic-resolution screenshots (720p in ~1,200 tokens vs ~4,000 for HTML).
eval_metrics: Benchmarks and metrics: WebArena task success rate (OOD self-hosted sites) for text agents; ScreenSpot Web grounding accuracy on text vs icon/widget instructions; Multimodal-Mind2Web Element Accuracy, Operation F1, and Step Success Rate across cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain splits for vision agents. Headline numbers: on WebArena, Qwen2.5-7B w/ AgentTrek scores 10.46 and Qwen2.5-32B w/ AgentTrek 22.40, beating GPT-4o (13.10) and GPT-4 (14.41). On ScreenSpot Web, Qwen2-VL-7B w/ AgentTrek reaches 81.7 text / 51.5 icon / 67.4 average, more than doubling the 30.7-average baseline and surpassing SeeClick (44.7) and CogAgent (50.7). On Multimodal-Mind2Web, AgentTrek+Mind2Web is best across all splits (e.g., cross-domain Step SR 52.6 vs 35.1 for Qwen2-VL alone). The VLM evaluator reaches 84% agreement with humans, and scaling from 20% to 100% of data lifts cross-domain Step SR from 39.5% to 45.0%.
key_results: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct fine-tuned on AgentTrek scores 22.40 success rate on WebArena, surpassing GPT-4 (14.41). Qwen2-VL-7B w/ AgentTrek reaches 67.4 average on ScreenSpot Web grounding vs 30.7 baseline. The fully automated pipeline produces verified multimodal trajectories at $0.551 each.
evolution_note: AgentTrek (2024, ICLR 2025) builds on the synthetic-trajectory trend for GUI agents (BAGEL, NNetNav, Synatra) and reacts against the cost and scalability limits of human-annotated datasets like Mind2Web, WebArena, and WebLINX. By turning freely available web tutorials into guided-replay demonstrations with a VLM evaluator, it establishes a low-cost automated data-synthesis paradigm that later scalable GUI-agent training efforts can build on or extend to dynamic, evolving websites.
